name: Washington
short: The US capital, Washington, D.C. In the news, shorthand for the American government.

name: Moscow
short: Russia's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Russian government.

1960.short: Capital of the Soviet Union. In the news, shorthand for the Soviet government.

name: Kyiv
short: Ukraine's capital, on the Dnipro river. In the news, shorthand for the Ukrainian government.

name: Beijing
short: China's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Chinese government.

name: Tehran
short: Iran's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Iranian government.

name: Taipei
short: Taiwan's capital. In the news, shorthand for Taiwan's government.

name: Tokyo
short: Japan's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Japanese government.

name: Manila
short: Capital of the Philippines. In the news, shorthand for the Philippine government.

name: Riyadh
short: Saudi Arabia's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Saudi government. Houthi missiles hit its main airport in October 2026.

name: Abu Dhabi
short: Capital of the United Arab Emirates, and in 2026 the venue of US-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks.

name: Cairo
short: Egypt's capital, the largest city in the Arab world. In the news, shorthand for the Egyptian government.

name: Caracas
short: Venezuela's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Venezuelan government.

name: Havana
short: Cuba's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Cuban government.

name: Islamabad
short: Pakistan's capital. In 2026 it briefly hosted a US-Iran framework that collapsed within weeks.

name: New Delhi
short: India's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Indian government.

name: Jerusalem
short: The city both Israel and the Palestinians claim as their capital; Israel's government sits there.
long: Israel annexed East Jerusalem after 1967, a move most countries do not recognise. In the news, 'Jerusalem' usually means the Israeli government.

name: Tel Aviv
short: Israel's largest city and business centre; many countries keep their embassies there.

name: Warsaw
short: Poland's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Polish government.

name: Berlin
short: Germany's capital. In the news, shorthand for the German government.

name: London
short: The UK capital. In the news, shorthand for the British government.

name: Paris
short: France's capital. In the news, shorthand for the French government.

name: Brussels
short: Belgium's capital, home of the EU institutions and NATO headquarters. In the news, often shorthand for the EU.

name: Ankara
short: Turkey's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Turkish government.

name: Canberra
short: Australia's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Australian government.

name: Baghdad
short: Iraq's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Iraqi government.

name: Kabul
short: Afghanistan's capital, under Taliban rule since August 2021.

name: Doha
short: Capital of Qatar, a frequent go-between in Middle East talks, from Gaza to Iran and Afghanistan.

name: Muscat
short: Capital of Oman, the quiet channel through which Washington, Tehran and the Houthis pass messages.

name: Sanaa
short: Yemen's historic capital, held by the Houthis since 2014.

name: Aden
short: Port city in southern Yemen, seat of the internationally recognised government since the Houthis took Sanaa.

name: Khartoum
short: Sudan's capital, where the Blue and White Nile meet; wrecked by fighting and retaken by the army in 2025.

name: Port Sudan
short: Sudan's main Red Sea port, where the army-led government moved after war engulfed Khartoum.

name: Addis Ababa
short: Ethiopia's capital and seat of the African Union.

name: Rawalpindi
short: City next to Islamabad that hosts Pakistan's army headquarters. In the news, shorthand for the military.

name: Mexico City
short: Mexico's capital. In the news, shorthand for the Mexican government.

name: Donetsk oblast
short: A region of eastern Ukraine, part of the industrial Donbas. Russia holds most of it and claims all of it.
long: Russian-backed separatists seized its capital, the city of Donetsk, in 2014. Russia claimed to annex the whole oblast in September 2022. Ukraine still holds the north-west, including the fortress belt, and says any withdrawal needs a referendum.

name: The fortress belt
short: Four fortified cities in Ukrainian-held Donetsk: Sloviansk, Kramatorsk, Druzhkivka and Kostiantynivka. Ukraine's strongest line in the east.
long: Fortified since 2014. Russia demands the whole of Donetsk in any deal; giving the belt up without a fight would leave open country between the front and the Dnipro.

name: Kramatorsk
short: An industrial city in Donetsk oblast, seat of Ukraine's regional government since 2014 and part of the fortress belt.

name: Sloviansk
short: A city in northern Donetsk oblast, held by Russian-backed fighters in 2014 until Ukraine retook it; anchor of the fortress belt.

name: Pokrovsk
short: A mining town and road hub in western Donetsk, focus of Russia's main offensive from 2024 and ruined by the fighting.

name: Huliaipole
short: A small town in Zaporizhzhia region on the southern front, under heavy Russian pressure since 2025.

name: Oleshky
short: A Russian-occupied town on the Dnipro's left bank near Kherson, site of a short local ceasefire in late October 2026.

name: Odesa
short: Ukraine's main Black Sea port, through which most of its grain exports leave; Russian nationalists have long coveted it.

name: Crimea
short: A Black Sea peninsula that Russia seized from Ukraine and annexed in 2014, a move most countries reject.

name: The Donbas
short: Ukraine's eastern coal and steel heartland, made up of Donetsk and Luhansk regions; fought over since 2014.

name: Lublin province
short: A region of eastern Poland bordering Ukraine and Belarus, where stray Russian drones have crossed into NATO airspace.

name: The Suwałki Gap
short: A 65 km strip of Polish-Lithuanian border between Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad: NATO's most exposed point.
long: If Russia closed it, the three Baltic states would be cut off by land from the rest of NATO. Military planners on both sides watch it closely.

name: Kaliningrad
short: A Russian enclave on the Baltic between Poland and Lithuania, heavily armed and home to nuclear-capable Iskander missiles.

name: Rostov-on-Don
short: Southern Russian city that hosts the headquarters running the war in Ukraine; Wagner mutineers seized it in 2023.

name: Buryatia
short: A poor Siberian republic near Mongolia that has sent a disproportionate share of Russia's soldiers to the war.

name: Alaska
short: The US state where Trump and Putin met in August 2025 for a summit on Ukraine that produced no deal.

name: Geneva
short: Swiss city that hosts UN agencies and many peace talks, including US-Ukraine rounds in 2025.

name: The Strait of Hormuz
short: The narrow sea lane between Iran and Oman through which about a fifth of the world's oil normally passes.
long: At its narrowest it is about 33 km wide. Iran has threatened for decades to close it; in 2026 it was closed and reopened as the US blockaded Iranian ports and the Revolutionary Guards attacked ships.

name: Fujairah
short: An Emirati port on the Gulf of Oman, outside Hormuz, built up so UAE oil could bypass the strait.

name: Jebel Ali
short: Dubai's giant container port, the busiest in the Middle East.

name: Dubai
short: The UAE's business and tourism hub, a trading gateway for Iran and much of the region.

name: Al Dhafra Air Base
short: An Emirati air base near Abu Dhabi that hosts US fighter jets and drones.

name: Taweelah
short: A coastal industrial zone near Abu Dhabi with one of the world's largest desalination plants, which supplies drinking water.

name: Abu Musa and the Tunbs
short: Three small Gulf islands near Hormuz that Iran has held since 1971 and the UAE still claims.

name: Isfahan
short: A historic Iranian city with a nuclear complex whose tunnels are believed to hold Iran's stock of 60% enriched uranium.
long: The IAEA's chief said in March 2026 that more than 200 kg of uranium enriched to 60% was likely intact there. Inspectors have had no access since February 2026.

name: Fordow
short: An Iranian uranium enrichment site buried inside a mountain near Qom, bombed by the US in June 2025.

name: Natanz
short: Iran's main uranium enrichment plant, partly underground, attacked repeatedly by Israel and the US.

name: Qom
short: Iran's holy city and centre of Shia scholarship, where senior clerics weigh in on the succession.

name: Bandar Abbas
short: Iran's main port on the Strait of Hormuz and a base for its navy and the Revolutionary Guards' fast boats.

name: Jask
short: A small Iranian port on the Gulf of Oman, outside Hormuz, that Tehran wants to turn into an oil and naval hub.

name: Larak Island
short: An Iranian island in the narrowest part of Hormuz, next to the shipping lanes, used by the Revolutionary Guards.

name: Bab al-Mandab
short: The strait between Yemen and Djibouti at the southern mouth of the Red Sea, on the route to the Suez Canal.
long: About 30 km wide. Around a tenth of world seaborne trade passed through before Houthi attacks from 2023 sent ships around Africa. In 2026 the Houthis pushed down the coast to the strait itself.

name: The Red Sea
short: The sea between Africa and Arabia linking the Suez Canal to the Indian Ocean, one of the world's busiest trade routes.

name: Perim
short: A small volcanic island in the middle of Bab al-Mandab. The Houthis reportedly seized it in 2026; this is not independently confirmed.

name: Mokha
short: A Red Sea port in Yemen, once famous for coffee, taken by the Houthis on 10 September 2026.

name: Dhubab
short: A coastal district at the mouth of the Red Sea, fought over in 2026 and retaken by government forces in October.

name: Khokha
short: A small Red Sea fishing town north of Mokha, a staging point for government forces.

name: Hodeidah
short: Yemen's main Red Sea port, held by the Houthis; most of the north's food and fuel comes through it.

name: Socotra
short: A Yemeni island in the Arabian Sea, famous for its unique plants, where the UAE built an airstrip and a military foothold.

name: Marib
short: An oil-producing province east of Sanaa, a long-held government and tribal stronghold against the Houthis.

name: Al-Bayda
short: A mountainous Yemeni province of powerful tribes, between Houthi-held north and the south.

name: Mukalla
short: Port capital of Yemen's eastern Hadramawt province on the Arabian Sea.

name: Ras Tanura
short: Saudi Arabia's largest oil export terminal and refinery, on the Gulf coast.

name: Yanbu
short: Saudi Red Sea port at the end of a pipeline that lets oil bypass Hormuz.

name: Jizan
short: Saudi province and port on the Yemeni border, often hit by Houthi fire.

name: King Khalid International Airport
short: Riyadh's main airport, struck by a Houthi missile on 10 October 2026 that killed 13 people.

name: NEOM
short: A planned $500bn futuristic city on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, flagship of Vision 2030.

name: Jeddah
short: Saudi Arabia's Red Sea port city, host of repeated talks between Sudan's warring sides.

name: The Suez Canal
short: Egypt's canal linking the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, a major source of hard currency for Cairo.
long: Before Houthi attacks began in late 2023, about 12% of world trade used it. Ships rerouting around Africa have cut Egypt's canal revenue by more than half.

name: The Cape of Good Hope
short: The southern tip of Africa: the long way round for ships avoiding the Red Sea, adding 10 to 14 days.

name: Somaliland
short: A self-declared state in northern Somalia on the Gulf of Aden, unrecognised by most countries, with an Emirati-run port.

name: Oman
short: A Gulf sultanate on the far side of Hormuz, trusted by both Washington and Tehran as a quiet mediator.

name: Qatar
short: A small, gas-rich Gulf state that hosts the largest US base in the region and mediates in many conflicts.

name: Bahrain
short: A Gulf island kingdom that hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet; Iran attacked US bases there in November 2026.

name: Eritrea
short: A closed, one-man-ruled state on the Red Sea that fought Ethiopia in 1998 to 2000; its troops are reported in Tigray again.

name: Libya
short: A North African oil state split between rival governments since 2014; its eastern strongman's airstrips feed Sudan's war.

name: Chad
short: Sudan's western neighbour; airstrips near the border are reported supply routes for the RSF.

name: El Fasher
short: Capital of North Darfur, taken by the RSF on 26 October 2025 after an 18-month siege, amid mass killings.

name: El Obeid
short: Capital of North Kordofan and gateway to the Nile valley, besieged by the RSF from July 2026.
long: Hundreds of thousands of civilians and two army divisions are inside. In November 2026 the army reportedly broke the siege; the city's fate decides whether the war moves east toward the Nile.

name: Nyala
short: Sudan's second city, in South Darfur, seat of the RSF's rival 'Tasis' government.

name: Kordofan
short: Sudan's central region between Darfur and the Nile, the war's main battlefield in 2026; famine is confirmed there.

name: Darfur
short: Western Sudan, scene of genocide in the 2000s; almost all of it is now held by the RSF.

name: Kosti
short: A White Nile river town on the main road west to El Obeid.

name: The Nile
short: The world's longest river, flowing north through Sudan and Egypt; Egypt gets almost all its water from it.

name: The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam
short: Africa's largest hydropower dam, on the Blue Nile in Ethiopia, inaugurated in 2025 over Egypt's objections.
long: Egypt fears Ethiopia can cut its water in a drought year; Ethiopia says the dam is about electricity, not control. Years of talks have produced no binding deal on how it is filled and run.

name: Lake Nasser
short: The huge reservoir behind Egypt's Aswan High Dam, the country's water bank.

name: Aswan
short: Southern Egyptian city by the High Dam, the first stop for many Sudanese refugees.

name: Ras El-Hekma
short: A Mediterranean headland the UAE agreed to develop for $35bn in 2024, a lifeline for Egypt's economy.

name: Tigray
short: Ethiopia's northern region, devastated by war from 2020 to 2022; fighting with the federal government resumed in 2026.

name: The Horn of Africa
short: The peninsula of north-east Africa: Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti and Somalia, facing Arabia across the Red Sea.

name: Miraflores Palace
short: The presidential palace in Caracas; in the news, shorthand for whoever holds power in Venezuela.

name: Fuerte Tiuna
short: Venezuela's main military complex in Caracas, home of the defence ministry; US forces struck it during the January 2026 raid.

name: Maiquetía
short: Site of Caracas's international airport, on the coast below the capital.

name: The Orinoco belt
short: A region of heavy oil along Venezuela's Orinoco river: on paper, the largest proven oil reserves on Earth.

name: The Florida Straits
short: The 150 km stretch of sea between Cuba and Florida, crossed by Cuban migrants on rafts in every crisis.

name: Morón
short: A town in central Cuba where protesters burned a Communist Party office in March 2026 during blackouts.

name: Santiago de Cuba
short: Cuba's second city, in the east, cradle of the 1959 revolution.

name: The Antonio Guiteras power plant
short: Cuba's largest oil-fired power station, near Matanzas; when it trips, much of the island goes dark.

name: Bejucal
short: A town south of Havana with a signals intelligence station that US officials say China uses to listen to the US.

name: Mariel
short: A Cuban port west of Havana, famous for the 1980 boatlift of 125,000 Cubans to Florida.

name: The Taiwan Strait
short: The 130 to 180 km wide sea between China and Taiwan, one of the world's busiest shipping lanes.

name: Keelung
short: Taiwan's main northern port, near Taipei; Chinese drills in December 2025 rehearsed sealing it off.

name: Kaohsiung
short: Taiwan's biggest port and second city, in the south; a main entry point for fuel.

name: Taichung
short: A city on Taiwan's west coast with a huge gas and coal power station and LNG terminal.

name: Penghu
short: A Taiwanese island group in the middle of the Taiwan Strait.

name: Xiamen
short: A Chinese port city facing Taiwan, a favourite venue for cross-strait contacts.

name: Hainan
short: China's southernmost province, an island hosting naval bases for the South China Sea.

name: Hokkaido
short: Japan's northern main island, a tourism and seafood region hit by Chinese boycotts.

name: Busan
short: South Korea's main port and second city.

name: The South China Sea
short: A sea of vital shipping lanes, fish and gas, almost all of which China claims against its neighbours.
long: An international tribunal in The Hague ruled in 2016 that China's sweeping claims have no legal basis. Beijing rejects the ruling and has built artificial islands with runways.

name: Scarborough Shoal
short: A reef and lagoon 220 km off the Philippine coast, under Chinese control since a 2012 standoff and claimed by both.
long: China calls it Huangyan Island. The 2016 Hague ruling said it is a traditional fishing ground for both. In June and July 2026 Chinese and Philippine ships faced off there again; Manila fears China will turn it into an artificial island.

name: Reed Bank
short: A submerged reef west of Palawan believed to hold large gas reserves, claimed by both the Philippines and China.

name: Malampaya
short: The Philippines' only major gas field, which powers much of Luzon and is running dry.

name: Zambales
short: A province on Luzon's west coast, the nearest Philippine land to Scarborough Shoal.

name: Luzon
short: The largest Philippine island, home to Manila and to several sites US forces can use.

name: Subic Bay
short: A deep-water bay on Luzon, a giant US naval base until 1992 and a shipyard and port today.

name: Davao
short: The biggest city on Mindanao, power base of the Duterte family.

name: Mindanao
short: The large southern Philippine island, home of the Duterte family's political base.

name: The Hague
short: Dutch city that hosts international courts: the ICC, the ICJ and the Permanent Court of Arbitration.

name: The Indus
short: The great river of Pakistan, rising in Tibet and flowing through Indian-held Kashmir; the basin feeds most of Pakistan's farms.

name: The Chenab
short: One of the Indus treaty's 'western rivers', reserved for Pakistan, flowing from Indian-held Jammu into Pakistani Punjab.

name: Baglihar and Salal dams
short: Two Indian hydropower dams on the Chenab whose gates let India time the river's flow into Pakistan.

name: Marala Headworks
short: The barrage where the Chenab enters Pakistan and feeds Punjab's irrigation canals.

name: Jammu
short: A city and region in Indian-administered Kashmir; Pakistan claims all of Kashmir.

name: Kashmir
short: A Himalayan region divided between India, Pakistan and China, claimed in full by India and Pakistan since 1947.

name: Pahalgam
short: A Kashmir resort town where gunmen killed 26 people, mostly tourists, on 22 April 2025.

name: Punjab
short: A fertile farming region split between India and Pakistan in 1947; Pakistan's breadbasket depends on Indus waters.

name: Lahore
short: Pakistan's second city and capital of its Punjab province, about 25 km from the Indian border.

name: Pathankot
short: An Indian Punjab town with a major air base near the Pakistani border.

name: Amritsar
short: An Indian Punjab city near the Pakistani border, home of the Sikh Golden Temple.

name: Mumbai
short: India's financial capital and largest city, home of its main stock exchanges.

name: Ladakh
short: A high-altitude Indian territory facing China, where the two armies clashed in 2020.

name: The Line of Control
short: The military line dividing Indian- and Pakistani-held Kashmir since 1972; not an agreed border.

name: The Line of Actual Control
short: The disputed, undemarcated line between Indian- and Chinese-held territory in the Himalayas.

name: Kurram
short: A tribal district of north-west Pakistan on the Afghan border, often hit by militant attacks.

name: The Brahmaputra
short: A great river rising in Tibet and flowing through India; China's dams upstream worry New Delhi.

name: Kandahar
short: Afghanistan's second city, birthplace of the Taliban and seat of its supreme leader.

name: The Gaza Strip
short: A 41 km coastal strip of about two million Palestinians, devastated by war since October 2023; a ceasefire holds, with violations.
long: Hamas ruled it from 2007. The war after its 7 October 2023 attack on Israel killed tens of thousands and destroyed most buildings. Under the October 2025 US-backed plan, a ceasefire holds with violations, Israeli troops control much of the strip and aid remains far below need.

name: The West Bank
short: Palestinian territory west of the Jordan river, occupied by Israel since 1967, with about 700,000 Israeli settlers.
long: Parts are run by the Palestinian Authority; Israel controls most of the land and security. Settler violence and military raids rose sharply after 2023, and Israeli ministers push to annex it.

name: Rafah
short: The southern Gaza town on the Egyptian border; its crossing is the strip's only gate not run by Israel.

name: Khan Younis
short: Southern Gaza's largest city, largely destroyed in the war.

name: Kerem Shalom
short: The main Israeli crossing for aid trucks into Gaza, where Israel, Egypt and Gaza meet.

name: Sinai
short: Egypt's desert peninsula bordering Israel and Gaza; Cairo refuses to let Gazans be pushed into it.

name: The Jordan Valley
short: The eastern strip of the West Bank along the Jordan river, which Israeli leaders want to keep or annex.

name: Greenland
short: The world's largest island, a self-governing part of Denmark, which Trump says the US should own.

name: Florida
short: The US state 150 km from Cuba, home of most Cuban and Venezuelan exiles and their politicians.

name: New York
short: The US city where Maduro is on trial in federal court and where the UN has its headquarters.

name: Miami
short: Florida city, capital of the Cuban and Venezuelan diasporas.
